text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamic summit calls on members to reconsider ties with Israel until it fulfills its obligations. Islamabad communique will denounce settlements in Jerusalem and the occupied lands.

- Four offers from international and local investors to set up projects in the New Valley, including the pumping station. Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib says Egypt has had offers from four institutions to market Egyptian bonds abroad.
- State offers workers in its agricultural companies 52,000 acres (21,044 hectares) in areas in western Nubariya and the Nile delta.
- Constitutional court approves central bank decision on not distributing profits to shareholders if its reserves are found lacking.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri approves 260 million pounds ($76.60 million) of emergency investments in the New Valley and Sinai. Government approves 160 million pounds to build infrastructure in north Sinai.
- First batch of Egyptian pilgrims arrive at Saudi port of Jeddah.
- Parliament approves new lease law for shops after it was approved by the cabinet.
- Bosnian prime minister to sign three treaties in Cairo today.
